We need propose 3-step retrosynthesis for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have hints: step1 forward: carboxylic acid to amide (coupling). So retrosynthetic step: break amide bond to give carboxylic acid and amine.

Step2 forward: Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (with decarboxylation). So retrosynthetic step: break C=C double bond and carboxylic acid to give aldehyde and malonic acid? Actually forward: aldehyde + malonic acid -> unsaturated acid. So reverse: unsaturated acid -> aldehyde + malonic acid (or maybe malonic acid fragment). So we need to identify that part: the fragment /C=C/C(=O)N... is an α,β-unsaturated amide after coupling? Wait target has /C=C/C(=O)N... So unsaturated amide attached to aromatic ring via double bond. The unsaturated acid precursor would be /C=C/COOH (cinnamic acid). Then coupling with aniline to give amide. So step1: amide formation between cinnamic acid derivative and aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). So retrosynthesis: break amide to give cinnamic acid (with double bond) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). The aniline is an aniline with an NH2 (para? Actually Nc3ccccc3N is an aniline with an extra NH? It's an aniline with an amino group attached to phenyl? Actually Nc3ccccc3N is an aniline where the nitrogen is attached to phenyl and also has an NH? It's a phenylamine (aniline) with an extra NH? The SMILES: Nc3ccccc3N means an aniline with an extra NH attached to the same N? Actually N attached to aromatic carbon and also has H (primary amine) and also attached to another N? Wait "Nc3ccccc3N": N attached to aromatic carbon (c3...), and also has H (since N is primary). The trailing N after the ring is attached to the same N? Actually SMILES: N c3 c c c c c3 N. That means N attached to aromatic carbon, and after the ring, there is N attached to the aromatic carbon? No, the second N is attached to the aromatic carbon as well? The pattern is N-Ph-N? Actually "Nc3ccccc3N" means an aniline where the nitrogen is attached to the phenyl ring at position 1, and there is also an N attached to the same carbon? No, the SMILES is ambiguous. But likely it's p-phenylenediamine? Actually p-phenylenediamine is "Nc1ccc(N)cc1". So "Nc3ccccc3N" is same as that: aniline with two amino groups on same ring? It's a benzene with two NH2 groups at positions 1 and maybe 1? Actually both attached to same carbon impossible. So it's likely a phenyl with two substituents: one N attached to the carbon (the first N) and the second N attached to the same carbon? Not possible. Might be a mistake but we treat as aniline (aniline with NH2). So step1 yields aniline (c3ccccc3N) and cinnamic acid (c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2). Actually the unsaturated acid attached to phenyl sulfonyl group? Wait the unsaturated part is attached to phenyl sulfonyl group: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 attached to sulfonyl group S(=O)(=O) to an aniline ring (first phenyl with methyl). So overall target: a sulfonamide linking two phenyl rings, one with methyl, the other with unsaturated amide attached to aniline.

Thus retrosynthesis steps:

Step3 forward: sulfonamide formation between an amine (the first phenyl with methyl, i.e., p-toluidine) and sulfonyl chloride derived from the second phenyl sulfonyl chloride (maybe from sulfonyl chloride of the second phenyl). In retrosynthesis, break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonic acid?) and amine. Typically sulfonamide formation: amine + sulfonyl chloride -> sulfonamide. So reverse: sulfonamide -> amine + sulfonyl chloride. So we can propose disconnection: target -> break S-N bond to give p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(N)cc1) and sulfonyl chloride of the other phenyl (ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(... )cc2). That sulfonyl chloride can be derived from sulfonylation of the phenyl with SO2Cl2 etc.

Thus three steps:

1. Amide formation: break C(=O)-N to give cinnamic acid (c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2) and aniline (c3ccccc3N).

2. Doebner modification: break C=C double bond and carboxylic acid to give aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(C=O)cc2) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). The aldehyde is the phenyl ring with aldehyde para? Actually the cinnamic acid derived from aldehyde at para position? The target phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2) has the unsaturated side chain at para position relative to sulfonyl? The SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the aldehyde precursor would be c2ccc(C=O)cc2 (para-aldehyde). So step2: break double bond and carboxyl to give that aldehyde and malonic acid.

3. Sulfonamide formation: break S-N to give p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(N)cc1) and sulfonyl chloride of the aldehyde phenyl (ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=O)cc2). The sulfonyl chloride can be made from the aldehyde phenyl via chlorosulfonation.

Thus we need to find template IDs for each transformation. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria for each.

First, amide formation: functional_groups_broken: ["aliphatic carboxylic acid"]? Actually amide formation breaks aliphatic carboxylic acid (C-O) and forms amide. So broken: aliphatic carboxylic acid, formed: amide. Use those.

Let's search.
